from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Imagine a magnifying glass sliding over data.", "This filter captures local pixel patterns.", "It slides, computes, and shifts sequentially."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Pixel grid
        pixel_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7, color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(36)])
        pixel_grid.arrange_in_grid(6, 6, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(pixel_grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Filter window
        window = Rectangle(width=2.3, height=2.3, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(window, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel_grid), FadeIn(window))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(window.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        path = VMobject()
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B2'], self.grid['B3'], self.grid['C3'], self.grid['C2']])
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(window, path), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Mechanics (The Sliding Dot Product)", [
            "Multiply filter values by underlying pixels.", 
            "Sum these values into one new pixel.", 
            "This defines a single discrete convolution."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        formula = MathTex(r"\sum", r"x_i", r"\cdot", r"w_i").scale(1.2)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Example grid elements (simplified representation)

        self.place_at_grid(dots.arrange(RIGHT), "D3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        res = MathTex("0.5").set_color(GREEN)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Local Influence", [
            "Each output pixel gathers local influence.",
            "Spatial information flows into synthesized results.",
            "Local neighborhoods determine output characteristics."
        ])
        
        # Grid representation
        input_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.8, stroke_color=GREY, stroke_width=2) for _ in range(9)])

        target_pixel = Square(side_length=0.8, fill_color="#ffcc00", fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_color=WHITE)
        target_pixel.move_to(input_grid[4].get_center())
        
        highlight_box = Square(side_length=2.4, stroke_color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        highlight_box.move_to(input_grid.get_center())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ffcc00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(input_grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(target_pixel))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00ffcc"))
        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#cc00ff"))
        arrow = Arrow(start=highlight_box.get_right() + RIGHT * 0.2, end=highlight_box.get_right() + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Edge Detector", [
            "Specific filters can detect edges.",
            "The Sobel operator highlights intensity changes.",
            "Images transform into structural sketches."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        kernel = Matrix([[-1, 0, 1], [-2, 0, 2], [-1, 0, 1]], 
                         h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.5).set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(kernel))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        # Representing an intensity grid
        grid_viz = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5).set_stroke(WHITE, 1) for _ in range(9)])
        grid_viz.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(grid_viz, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_viz))
        self.play(kernel.animate.move_to(grid_viz.get_center()))
        self.play(grid_viz.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        result_text = Text("Edge Map", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(result_text, 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(result_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Impact: Neural Networks", [
            "CNNs learn these filter patterns automatically.",
            "Edges form the foundation for features.",
            "Filters stack to recognize complex objects."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing automatic filter learning
        layer_1 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(layer_1, 'B2')
        label_1 = Text("Layer 1: Edges", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, 'B2').shift(DOWN * 1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(layer_1), Write(label_1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Representing stacking for features
        layer_2 = Square(side_length=1.2, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(layer_2, 'B4')
        label_2 = Text("Layer 2: Textures", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2, 'B4').shift(DOWN * 1.0)
        
        arrow = Arrow(layer_1.get_right(), layer_2.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(layer_2), GrowArrow(arrow), Write(label_2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final recognition
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'B6')
        label_3 = Text("Object: Dog", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_3, 'B6').shift(DOWN * 1.0)
        
        arrow2 = Arrow(layer_2.get_right(), dot.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), GrowArrow(arrow2), Write(label_3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Data Science students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a 'filter' sliding over data. Use an analogy of a magnifying glass moving across a grid, where each step computes a weighted average of local neighbors.
sections.example: A 3x3 'filter' sliding over a pixelated photo of a Cat's face, blurring the edges as it moves.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (The Sliding Dot Product)
sections.content: Define discrete convolution as the element-wise multiplication of the filter and the underlying input, followed by a summation. Use a visual grid animation showing values multiplying and collapsing into a single output pixel.
sections.example: A 3x3 matrix multiplication: Input [1, 0, 1] * Filter [0.5, 1, 0.5] = Output value 0.5.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Local Influence
sections.content: Briefly explain that every output pixel is a 'synthesis' of its immediate surroundings. This prepares the learner to understand how spatial information is preserved or transformed.
sections.example: Visualizing how changing one central pixel in the input affects exactly 9 pixels in the resulting convolution.

sections.title: Application: The Edge Detector
sections.content: Demonstrate how specific filters (kernels) change the image. Introduce the Sobel operator as a way to highlight sudden changes in intensity.
sections.example: An animation transforming a grayscale photo of a Robot into a glowing white-line sketch against a black background.

sections.title: Real-World Impact: Neural Networks
sections.content: Conclude by bridging the gap to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Explain that 'training' a model is simply learning the best filter values to detect complex patterns like whiskers or ears.
sections.example: A flowchart showing layers of convolutions: first detecting edges, then textures, and finally recognizing the full face of a Golden Retriever.
